document.abstract: Centralcasting is steadily gaining momentum among television station groups that see it as a practical, cost-saving operating philosophy; however, an often-overlooked risk exists that is so significant that its costs may far outweigh any savings realized from the reduction of staff and consolidation of capital equipment. This risk lies in a lack of redundancy and, hence, reliability of the router in a typical central-casting model. This paper discusses the potential risk and suggests a solution that, although appearing contrary to the very notion of centralization, is ideally suited for centralized operations and provides true risk mitigation in signal distribution between central and remote sites.

authors.bio: Michael W. Schmid is currently product marketing manager, routing and distribution for Leitch Technology Corp., and in this capacity is responsible for the direction and implementation of the global marketing strategy for routing and distribution products. A former Lieutenant in the U.S. Navy, Schmid held an impressive array of increasingly responsible management positions before joining Leitch in July 1996 as marketing research manager. He brought to Leitch extensive experience in product management, strategic planning, and marketing. Schmid holds a B.A. degree in German and an MBA degree from Old Dominion University. A former president of the American Marketing Association, he is currently on the board of directors of the Old Dominion University Alumni Association, and is a member of the NAB Exhibit Advisory Committee and SMPTE.
